class Mike21Driver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the DHI Mike21 ``.mesh`` frame format.

    Plain text despite the DHI name, so it needs no dependency. A header line, then one
    record per node, then an element header, then one record per element. The format
    carries a mesh frame and no results, so the driver declares ``read_mesh`` only.

    Node elevation becomes a ``node_z`` variable, as it does for 2DM: the pyramids mesh
    model is planar and carries no per-node elevation coordinate (design section 6). The
    file's z column is read as written, never fabricated.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The projection field and the node-record column order are read as the
          format specifies, but could not be checked against a vendor file.** If a real Mike21
          mesh orders its node columns differently, the coordinates would be wrong in a
          plausible way; this is the part of the driver a vendor sample should confirm.
        - **The projection is mapped to a CRS only when it is real.** A WKT string or an
          EPSG code that the vendored PROJ validates is carried; a DHI-internal name
          such as ``UTM-32`` or ``LONG/LAT`` carries no datum and leaves ``crs`` as
          ``None`` rather than being guessed at.
        - The boundary code in each node record is **not carried**. It marks open and
          land boundaries, which this package has nowhere to put on a bare frame; it is
          dropped rather than turned into a variable the mesh model would not recognise.
        - A triangle in a quad mesh is padded with a trailing ``0`` node id. Since ids
          are 1-based, ``0`` is read as fill and becomes ``-1`` padding, never node
          index zero.
        - Node ids are resolved through an id map rather than assumed contiguous, so a
          renumbered file is wired correctly; the 1-based numbering is recorded for a
          writer to restore.

    Examples:
        - Write the smallest valid Mike21 mesh and read it back. The unit square's two
          triangles come through as a 2D mesh, and the 1-based ids arrive 0-based with
          the file's base recorded for a writer:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.misc import (
            ...     Mike21Driver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.mesh")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21(path)
            ...     dataset = Mike21Driver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (4, 2)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2, 3]]
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.original_start_index
            1

        - Elevation comes back as a node variable, because the mesh model carries no
          per-node elevation coordinate:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.misc import (
            ...     Mike21Driver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.mesh")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21(path)
            ...     dataset = Mike21Driver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.data_variable_names
            ['node_z']
            >>> dataset.get("node_z").location
            'node'

        - A DHI-internal projection name carries no datum, so the CRS is left unset
          rather than guessed:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.misc import (
            ...     Mike21Driver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.mesh")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21(path)
            ...     dataset = Mike21Driver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.crs_wkt is None
            True
    """

    name = "mike21"
    long_name = "DHI Mike21 mesh"
    suffixes = (".mesh",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "write_mesh", "write_data"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the first line parses as a Mike21 header.

        The header is ``<item> <unit> <node_count> <projection...>``, so a readable
        first line whose third field is a positive integer is the cheapest signature
        the format offers. A binary file decodes to replacement characters and fails
        that test rather than raising.

        ``.mesh`` is a common suffix, so the sniff is what keeps a foreign ``.mesh``
        file -- a 3D model export, say -- from being claimed. It is still only a header
        shape: a file that passes it but breaks later is refused by ``read``, which is
        why the two must not disagree about what a header looks like.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the first line has the header's shape.
        """
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            first = handle.readline(4096)
        tokens = first.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace").split()
        if len(tokens) < _ELEMENT_HEADER_FIELDS + 1:
            return False
        try:
            return int(tokens[2]) > 0
        except ValueError:
            return False

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a Mike21 ``.mesh`` file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ``.mesh`` file to read.
            lazy: Ignored -- the format is plain text and read eagerly.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, faces and the ``node_z`` elevation variable.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file is empty, a record is short of its
                columns, a count does not match the records that follow, or a numeric
                field is not a number.
            ValueError: If an element references a node id the file never defined, or
                two nodes share an id.
        """
        return _Mike21Scan(path).build()

    def write(self, dataset, path: str, **options) -> None:
        """Write a mesh frame back to a Mike21 ``.mesh`` file.

        Emits the header line, one ``id x y z boundary`` record per node and one
        ``id n1 n2 n3[ n4]`` record per element, restoring the 1-based numbering the
        reader recorded. Node elevation comes from a node-located ``node_z`` variable when
        present, else ``0``; a triangle in a quad-width table is padded with a trailing
        ``0`` node id, the format's own convention.

        The EUM item and unit codes, the per-node boundary code and the element type code
        are not carried on the mesh model, so they are written as documented defaults; the
        reader does not read them back. A real CRS (EPSG or WKT) is written as the
        projection field, else the DHI-internal ``LONG/LAT`` placeholder.

        Args:
            dataset: The :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` to write.
            path: The output ``.mesh`` path.
            **options: Unused; accepted for a uniform writer signature.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the dataset carries no faces, or any face has
                a vertex count other than 3 or 4 (Mike21 has only triangle and quad
                element types).
        """
        mesh = dataset.mesh
        connectivity = mesh.face_node_connectivity
        if connectivity is None or connectivity.data is None:
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                f"cannot write {path!r}: the dataset has no face connectivity to write "
                f"as a Mike21 mesh"
            )
        faces = np.asarray(connectivity.data)
        base = connectivity.original_start_index
        if base is None:
            base = 1
        real_counts = (
            np.sum(faces != -1, axis=1)
            if faces.ndim == 2
            else np.array([np.sum(faces != -1)])
        )
        unsupported = sorted(
            {int(c) for c in np.unique(real_counts) if c not in (3, 4)}
        )
        if unsupported:
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
                f"cannot write {path!r}: Mike21 has only triangle (3) and quad (4) "
                f"elements, but the mesh has face(s) with {unsupported} vertices"
            )
        node_x = np.asarray(mesh.node_x, dtype=np.float64)
        node_y = np.asarray(mesh.node_y, dtype=np.float64)
        node_z = _writer_node_z(dataset, len(node_x))
        max_nodes = faces.shape[1] if faces.ndim == 2 else 3
        type_code = _MIKE21_ELEMENT_TYPE.get(max_nodes, _MIKE21_ELEMENT_TYPE[3])
        projection = _crs_to_projection(dataset)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(
                f"{_DEFAULT_ITEM} {_DEFAULT_UNIT} {len(node_x)} {projection}\n"
            )
            for index in range(len(node_x)):
                z = 0.0 if node_z is None else float(node_z[index])
                handle.write(
                    f"{index + base} {float(node_x[index])!r} "
                    f"{float(node_y[index])!r} {z!r} {_DEFAULT_BOUNDARY}\n"
                )
            handle.write(f"{len(faces)} {max_nodes} {type_code}\n")
            for row_index, row in enumerate(faces):
                vertices = [int(v) + base for v in row if int(v) != -1]
                padded = vertices + [_ELEMENT_PADDING] * (max_nodes - len(vertices))
                ids = " ".join(str(v) for v in padded)
                handle.write(f"{row_index + base} {ids}\n")

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path, unused by the single-mesh default.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The configured mesh name, as a one-item list.

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.text:
Write a mesh frame back to a Mike21 .mesh file.

Emits the header line, one id x y z boundary record per node and one id n1 n2 n3[ n4] record per element, restoring the 1-based numbering the reader recorded. Node elevation comes from a node-located node_z variable when present, else 0; a triangle in a quad-width table is padded with a trailing 0 node id, the format's own convention.

The EUM item and unit codes, the per-node boundary code and the element type code are not carried on the mesh model, so they are written as documented defaults; the reader does not read them back. A real CRS (EPSG or WKT) is written as the projection field, else the DHI-internal LONG/LAT placeholder.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset

The :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset to write.

required path str

The output .mesh path.

required **options

Unused; accepted for a uniform writer signature.

{}

Raises:

Type Description FileFormatNotSupportedError

If the dataset carries no faces, or any face has a vertex count other than 3 or 4 (Mike21 has only triangle and quad element types).

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/drivers/misc.py 
def write(self, dataset, path: str, **options) -> None:
    """Write a mesh frame back to a Mike21 ``.mesh`` file.

    Emits the header line, one ``id x y z boundary`` record per node and one
    ``id n1 n2 n3[ n4]`` record per element, restoring the 1-based numbering the
    reader recorded. Node elevation comes from a node-located ``node_z`` variable when
    present, else ``0``; a triangle in a quad-width table is padded with a trailing
    ``0`` node id, the format's own convention.

    The EUM item and unit codes, the per-node boundary code and the element type code
    are not carried on the mesh model, so they are written as documented defaults; the
    reader does not read them back. A real CRS (EPSG or WKT) is written as the
    projection field, else the DHI-internal ``LONG/LAT`` placeholder.

    Args:
        dataset: The :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` to write.
        path: The output ``.mesh`` path.
        **options: Unused; accepted for a uniform writer signature.

    Raises:
        FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the dataset carries no faces, or any face has
            a vertex count other than 3 or 4 (Mike21 has only triangle and quad
            element types).
    """
    mesh = dataset.mesh
    connectivity = mesh.face_node_connectivity
    if connectivity is None or connectivity.data is None:
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"cannot write {path!r}: the dataset has no face connectivity to write "
            f"as a Mike21 mesh"
        )
    faces = np.asarray(connectivity.data)
    base = connectivity.original_start_index
    if base is None:
        base = 1
    real_counts = (
        np.sum(faces != -1, axis=1)
        if faces.ndim == 2
        else np.array([np.sum(faces != -1)])
    )
    unsupported = sorted(
        {int(c) for c in np.unique(real_counts) if c not in (3, 4)}
    )
    if unsupported:
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"cannot write {path!r}: Mike21 has only triangle (3) and quad (4) "
            f"elements, but the mesh has face(s) with {unsupported} vertices"
        )
    node_x = np.asarray(mesh.node_x, dtype=np.float64)
    node_y = np.asarray(mesh.node_y, dtype=np.float64)
    node_z = _writer_node_z(dataset, len(node_x))
    max_nodes = faces.shape[1] if faces.ndim == 2 else 3
    type_code = _MIKE21_ELEMENT_TYPE.get(max_nodes, _MIKE21_ELEMENT_TYPE[3])
    projection = _crs_to_projection(dataset)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(
            f"{_DEFAULT_ITEM} {_DEFAULT_UNIT} {len(node_x)} {projection}\n"
        )
        for index in range(len(node_x)):
            z = 0.0 if node_z is None else float(node_z[index])
            handle.write(
                f"{index + base} {float(node_x[index])!r} "
                f"{float(node_y[index])!r} {z!r} {_DEFAULT_BOUNDARY}\n"
            )
        handle.write(f"{len(faces)} {max_nodes} {type_code}\n")
        for row_index, row in enumerate(faces):
            vertices = [int(v) + base for v in row if int(v) != -1]
            padded = vertices + [_ELEMENT_PADDING] * (max_nodes - len(vertices))
            ids = " ".join(str(v) for v in padded)
            handle.write(f"{row_index + base} {ids}\n")

docs.title: MODFLOW 6 DISV
docs.text:
Reader for the MODFLOW 6 DISV (discretization by vertices) grid (task C5).

MODFLOW 6's DISV package describes a layered groundwater grid whose horizontal footprint is an unstructured set of polygonal cells. This driver reads the recommended ASCII .disv input file — one file of a MODFLOW 6 model directory — and builds that single horizontal cell layer as a surface mesh.

Driver name modflow6_disv Suffixes .disv (the ASCII grid input of a MODFLOW 6 model) Capabilities read_mesh

docs.title: The ASCII grammar
docs.text:
Three keyword blocks matter; the intervening GRIDDATA block (TOP/BOTM/IDOMAIN) is skipped:

BEGIN DIMENSIONS
  NLAY <nlay>        number of layers
  NCPL <ncpl>        number of cells per layer -- the face count
  NVERT <nvert>      number of vertices -- the node count
END DIMENSIONS

BEGIN VERTICES
  <iv> <x> <y>       one 1-based vertex per line
END VERTICES

BEGIN CELL2D
  <icell2d> <xc> <yc> <ncvert> <icvert...>   1-based vertex ids, clockwise
END CELL2D

VERTICES becomes node_x / node_y; each CELL2D row's icvert list becomes one fill-padded, 1-based face row; xc / yc become the face centres.

docs.title: Dispatch
docs.text:
A .disv file dispatches by its suffix; can_open confirms the DISV blocks are present rather than only matching the name:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("model/tri_model.disv", driver="modflow6_disv")
footprint = mesh.mesh      # NCPL polygons, one horizontal layer

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• One horizontal layer. A DISV grid is NLAY layers sharing a single horizontal footprint of NCPL cells; the mesh is that footprint. The vertical layering and the TOP / BOTM / IDOMAIN arrays in GRIDDATA are not modelled — this package reads the mesh file format, not the full groundwater model.
  • ASCII only (for now). The binary companion grid .disv.grb (ASCII header GRID DISV, a text metadata block naming the arrays, then binary VERTICES / IAVERT / JAVERT) is not read in v1. The driver claims only the .disv suffix, so a lone .grb is not dispatched to it. Reading the binary grid as a fallback when only it is present is a possible future addition.
  • Vertex ids are 1-based. They are resolved to 0-based and the base recorded for a writer. A short (polygonal) face row is padded; a triangular grid has no padding.
  • Cells are clockwise. DISV lists icvert clockwise; pyramids reverses each face to counter-clockwise on read.
  • There is no CRS or node elevation in a .disv file, so crs and node_z are None; the cell centres are carried as the face centres.

docs.title: MODFLOW 6 DISU
docs.text:
Reader for the MODFLOW 6 DISU (discretization by unstructured) grid.

MODFLOW 6's DISU package describes a fully-unstructured groundwater grid by its connection graph. When the grid also declares vertices, its horizontal footprint is an unstructured set of polygonal cells — identical in shape to a DISV grid. This driver reads the ASCII .disu input file and builds that footprint as a surface mesh; it reuses the DISV block-parsing helpers and refuses a connectivity-only DISU, which carries no geometry.

Driver name modflow6_disu Suffixes .disu (the ASCII grid input of a MODFLOW 6 model) Capabilities read_mesh Returns MeshDataset

docs.title: The ASCII grammar
docs.text:
DISU shares DISV's BEGIN/END block grammar. The geometry lives in three blocks; the GRIDDATA and CONNECTIONDATA blocks are skipped:

BEGIN DIMENSIONS
  NODES <nodes>      number of cells -- the face count
  NJA   <nja>        length of the connection vector (the DISU signature)
  NVERT <nvert>      number of vertices -- the node count (0 when geometry is absent)
END DIMENSIONS

BEGIN VERTICES
  <iv> <x> <y>       one 1-based vertex per line
END VERTICES

BEGIN CELL2D
  <icell2d> <xc> <yc> <ncvert> <icvert...>   1-based vertex ids, clockwise
END CELL2D

VERTICES becomes node_x / node_y; each CELL2D row's icvert list becomes one fill-padded, 1-based face row; xc / yc become the face centres. A VERTICES or CELL2D block may defer its rows to an external file with an OPEN/CLOSE <fname> directive, which is read relative to the .disu file.

docs.title: Dispatch
docs.text:
A .disu file dispatches by its suffix; can_open confirms the DISU DIMENSIONS block (NODES and NJA) is present rather than only matching the name:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("model/keating.disu", driver="modflow6_disu")
footprint = mesh.mesh      # NODES polygons, one horizontal footprint

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Vertices required. A connectivity-only DISU (NVERT absent or zero, no VERTICES / CELL2D) has no geometry to place; it is refused with a clear error rather than approximated from the connection graph.
  • One horizontal footprint. The mesh is the NODES cells of CELL2D. The GRIDDATA arrays (TOP / BOT / AREA / IDOMAIN) and the CONNECTIONDATA connection graph are not modelled — this package reads the mesh file format, not the full groundwater model.
  • ASCII only. The binary .disu.grb grid is not read; point the reader at the ASCII .disu input.
  • Vertex ids are 1-based. They are resolved to 0-based and the base recorded for a writer. Short (polygonal) face rows are padded; the quad test fixture pads nothing.
  • Cells are clockwise. DISU lists icvert clockwise; pyramids reverses each face to counter-clockwise on read.
  • There is no CRS or node elevation in a .disu file, so crs and node_z are None; the cell centres are carried as the face centres.

docs.title: pyramids_mesh.drivers.modflow.Modflow6DisuDriver
docs.text:
Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the MODFLOW 6 DISU (discretization by unstructured) ASCII grid.

The .disu file is one file of a MODFLOW 6 model directory. read_file dispatches to this driver on the .disu suffix, and can_open confirms the file carries the DISU NODES / NJA dimensions rather than only matching the name.

A DISU grid is defined by its connection graph (NJA / CONNECTIONDATA) and need not carry any geometry. When it does declare NVERT > 0 with VERTICES and CELL2D blocks, its horizontal footprint is identical in shape to a DISV grid, so this driver reuses the DISV block-parsing helpers and builds the NODES polygonal cells as a surface mesh. A connectivity-only DISU -- no NVERT, no VERTICES / CELL2D -- carries no coordinates and is refused with a clear error rather than guessed.

Documented limitations
  • Vertices required. A connectivity-only DISU (NVERT absent or zero, no VERTICES / CELL2D) has no geometry to place; it is refused rather than approximated from the connection graph.
  • One horizontal footprint. The mesh is the NODES cells of the CELL2D block. The GRIDDATA arrays (TOP / BOT / AREA / IDOMAIN) and the CONNECTIONDATA connection graph are not modelled -- this package reads the mesh file format, not the full groundwater model.
  • ASCII only. The binary .disu.grb grid is not read; point the reader at the ASCII .disu input.
  • Vertex ids are 1-based. They are resolved to 0-based and the base recorded for a writer. Short (polygonal) face rows are padded; the quad test fixture pads nothing.
  • Cells are clockwise. DISU lists icvert clockwise, like DISV; pyramids reverses each face to counter-clockwise on read.
  • OPEN/CLOSE is honoured. A VERTICES or CELL2D block may defer its rows to an external file with an OPEN/CLOSE <fname> directive; the external file is read relative to the .disu file. The committed sample is inline.
  • There is no CRS or node elevation in a .disu file, so crs and node_z are None; the cell centres are carried as the face centres.
Example

Read a MODFLOW 6 DISU grid by its .disu file (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real DISU file)::

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("model/keating.disu", driver="modflow6_disu")
footprint = mesh.mesh      # NODES polygons, one horizontal footprint

class Modflow6DisuDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the MODFLOW 6 DISU (discretization by unstructured) ASCII grid.

    The ``.disu`` file is one file of a MODFLOW 6 model directory. ``read_file`` dispatches
    to this driver on the ``.disu`` suffix, and ``can_open`` confirms the file carries the
    DISU ``NODES`` / ``NJA`` dimensions rather than only matching the name.

    A DISU grid is defined by its connection graph (``NJA`` / ``CONNECTIONDATA``) and need
    not carry any geometry. When it *does* declare ``NVERT`` > 0 with ``VERTICES`` and
    ``CELL2D`` blocks, its horizontal footprint is identical in shape to a DISV grid, so
    this driver reuses the DISV block-parsing helpers and builds the ``NODES`` polygonal
    cells as a surface mesh. A connectivity-only DISU -- no ``NVERT``, no ``VERTICES`` /
    ``CELL2D`` -- carries no coordinates and is refused with a clear error rather than
    guessed.

    Documented limitations:
        - **Vertices required.** A connectivity-only DISU (``NVERT`` absent or zero, no
          ``VERTICES`` / ``CELL2D``) has no geometry to place; it is refused rather than
          approximated from the connection graph.
        - **One horizontal footprint.** The mesh is the ``NODES`` cells of the ``CELL2D``
          block. The ``GRIDDATA`` arrays (``TOP`` / ``BOT`` / ``AREA`` / ``IDOMAIN``) and
          the ``CONNECTIONDATA`` connection graph are not modelled -- this package reads
          the mesh file format, not the full groundwater model.
        - **ASCII only.** The binary ``.disu.grb`` grid is not read; point the reader at
          the ASCII ``.disu`` input.
        - **Vertex ids are 1-based.** They are resolved to 0-based and the base recorded
          for a writer. Short (polygonal) face rows are padded; the quad test fixture pads
          nothing.
        - **Cells are clockwise.** DISU lists ``icvert`` clockwise, like DISV; pyramids
          reverses each face to counter-clockwise on read.
        - **``OPEN/CLOSE`` is honoured.** A ``VERTICES`` or ``CELL2D`` block may defer its
          rows to an external file with an ``OPEN/CLOSE <fname>`` directive; the external
          file is read relative to the ``.disu`` file. The committed sample is inline.
        - There is no CRS or node elevation in a ``.disu`` file, so ``crs`` and ``node_z``
          are ``None``; the cell centres are carried as the face centres.

    Example:
        Read a MODFLOW 6 DISU grid by its ``.disu`` file (shown, not run as a doctest -- it
        needs a real DISU file)::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

            mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("model/keating.disu", driver="modflow6_disu")
            footprint = mesh.mesh      # NODES polygons, one horizontal footprint
    """

    name = "modflow6_disu"
    long_name = "MODFLOW 6 DISU"
    suffixes = (".disu",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file carries the DISU dimensions, not only the suffix.

        Reads the whole file -- a DISU grid is small -- and accepts it on the DISU
        signature: a ``DIMENSIONS`` block carrying both ``NODES`` and ``NJA``. ``NJA`` is
        what tells a DISU grid apart from a DISV one (which never declares it), so a stray
        or empty ``.disu`` is declined. A connectivity-only DISU still sniffs ``True`` --
        it is a real DISU grid -- and is refused later, in ``_parse``, with a clear
        message about the missing geometry.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the DISU ``DIMENSIONS`` block with ``NODES`` and ``NJA`` is
                present.
        """
        try:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                text = handle.read().upper()
        except OSError:
            return False
        return f"{_BEGIN} {_DIMENSIONS}" in text and _NODES in text and _NJA in text

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a ``.disu`` file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ``.disu`` file.
            lazy: Unused -- a DISU grid is small and read whole.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: The horizontal cell footprint, 1-based and clockwise as written.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the path is not a file, the grid is
                connectivity-only (no vertices to place), or the DISU blocks are missing,
                malformed, or disagree with the declared dimensions.
        """
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(f"{path!r} is not a MODFLOW 6 DISU file")
        return _Modflow6DisuReader(path).build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override
    this to read the names from the file.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path, unused by the single-mesh default.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The configured mesh name, as a one-item list.

    Examples:
        - A single-mesh driver names one topology, so the list it returns is the
          set of values ``read``'s ``mesh_name`` will accept:

            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> TinyDriver().mesh_names("anything.tiny")
            ['mesh2d']
    """
    return [self._default_mesh_name]

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: MPAS — spherical Voronoi NetCDF grid
docs.text:
The MPAS reader. MPAS (Model for Prediction Across Scales) writes its unstructured grid as NetCDF with Conventions = "MPAS". The grid is a spherical centroidal Voronoi tessellation: a hex-dominant primal mesh of cells and a dual mesh whose vertices are the Voronoi corners. This driver reads the dual — the corners become the mesh nodes and each primal cell becomes a face listing the corners around it. The file is read through the vendored GDAL multidimensional API (no declared dependency).

Driver name mpas Suffixes .nc Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns MeshDataset

An MPAS grid is not UGRID, so read_file reaches the driver through its NetCDF-suffix fallback:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("mesh.QU.1920km.nc")
mesh.mesh.n_node          # the Voronoi dual vertices
mesh.mesh.n_face          # the primal (hex-dominant) cells

The corner table per cell is verticesOnCell, a (nCells, maxEdges) array that is 1-based and padded with 0, with nEdgesOnCell giving each cell's valid count. Subtracting one and dropping the padding yields fill-padded, mixed-degree face-node connectivity: a coarse quasi-uniform mesh is 12 pentagons among hexagons, so the face table carries both 5- and 6-node rows.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Longitude/latitude are exposed, in degrees, not the Cartesian xVertex/yVertex. MPAS stores both: lon/lat (radians) and the 3D Cartesian coordinates on the sphere. Dropping z from the Cartesian triple collapses the two hemispheres onto one another and degenerates the cells at the limb, so the geographic coordinates are used instead and converted from radians to the conventional degrees. A cell straddling the antimeridian unwraps to a wide planar polygon — inherent to flattening a global mesh — but its winding is still well defined.
  • No CRS. The grid lives on a unit sphere (sphere_radius = 1) with no EPSG authority, so crs is None rather than guessed at 4326 (a WGS84 ellipsoid the mesh is not on).
  • The primal (hex) cells are the faces; the dual vertices are the nodes. Only the topology needed for that is read — coordinates and verticesOnCell. The many other MPAS fields (cellsOnCell, edge tables, areas, quality metrics) are not shipped as variables; this driver declares read_mesh only.
  • verticesOnCell is 1-based with 0 padding — resolved to 0-based, the base 1 recorded for a writer.

The mesh nodes are the dual vertices (lonVertex/latVertex) and each face is a primal cell, listing the dual vertices around it from verticesOnCell. Documented limitations

Dropping z from the Cartesian triple collapses the two hemispheres onto one another and degenerates the cells at the limb, so the geographic coordinates are used instead. They are carried verbatim in radians: converting to degrees is a projection concern that belongs in the GIS layer upstream (pyramids), not in a file-format driver -- the same rule the ICON reader follows. A cell straddling the antimeridian unwraps to a wide planar polygon -- inherent to flattening a global mesh -- but its winding is still well defined.
  • No CRS. The grid lives on a unit sphere (sphere_radius = 1) with no EPSG authority, so crs is None rather than guessed at 4326 (a WGS84 ellipsoid the mesh is not on).
  • The primal (hex) cells are the faces; the dual vertices are the nodes. Only the topology needed for that is read -- coordinates and verticesOnCell. The many other MPAS fields (cellsOnCell, edge tables, areas, quality metrics) are not shipped as variables; this driver declares read_mesh only.
  • verticesOnCell is 1-based with 0 padding -- resolved to 0-based and the base 1 recorded for a writer.
Example

Read an MPAS grid (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real NetCDF file), reached through read_file's NetCDF fallback::

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("mesh.QU.1920km.nc")
mesh.mesh.n_node          # the Voronoi dual vertices
mesh.mesh.n_face          # the primal (hex-dominant) cells
