class MpasDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for MPAS NetCDF grids -- the Voronoi dual as a mixed-degree mesh.

    The mesh nodes are the dual vertices (``lonVertex``/``latVertex``) and each face is a
    primal cell, listing the dual vertices around it from ``verticesOnCell``. That table
    is 1-based and ``0``-padded, with ``nEdgesOnCell`` giving each cell's valid corner
    count; subtracting one and dropping the padding gives fill-padded, mixed-degree
    face-node connectivity (5- and 6-node faces in a hex-dominant mesh).

    Documented limitations:
        - **Longitude/latitude are exposed, in the file's native radians, not the
          Cartesian ``xVertex``/``yVertex``.** MPAS stores both: lon/lat (radians) and the
          3D Cartesian coordinates on the sphere. Dropping ``z`` from the Cartesian triple
          collapses the two hemispheres onto one another and degenerates the cells at the
          limb, so the geographic coordinates are used instead. They are carried verbatim
          in radians: converting to degrees is a projection concern that belongs in the
          GIS layer upstream (pyramids), not in a file-format driver -- the same rule the
          ICON reader follows. A cell straddling the antimeridian unwraps to a wide planar
          polygon -- inherent to flattening a global mesh -- but its winding is still well
          defined.
        - **No CRS.** The grid lives on a unit sphere (``sphere_radius = 1``) with no EPSG
          authority, so ``crs`` is ``None`` rather than guessed at ``4326`` (a WGS84
          ellipsoid the mesh is not on).
        - **The primal (hex) cells are the faces; the dual vertices are the nodes.** Only
          the topology needed for that is read -- coordinates and ``verticesOnCell``. The
          many other MPAS fields (``cellsOnCell``, edge tables, areas, quality metrics)
          are not shipped as variables; this driver declares ``read_mesh`` only.
        - **``verticesOnCell`` is 1-based with ``0`` padding** -- resolved to 0-based and
          the base ``1`` recorded for a writer.

    Example:
        Read an MPAS grid (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real NetCDF file),
        reached through ``read_file``'s NetCDF fallback::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

            mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("mesh.QU.1920km.nc")
            mesh.mesh.n_node          # the Voronoi dual vertices
            mesh.mesh.n_face          # the primal (hex-dominant) cells
    """

    name = "mpas"
    long_name = "MPAS mesh"
    suffixes = (".nc",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is an MPAS grid.

        Keyed on ``Conventions`` containing ``MPAS`` *and* the presence of
        ``verticesOnCell``, so a plain NetCDF, a UGRID mesh, or another model's ``.nc``
        (3Di, TUFLOW FV) is not claimed. Opening a non-NetCDF file raises inside GDAL and
        is reported as "not MPAS" rather than propagated.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the MPAS convention and corner table are both present.
        """
        with gdal.ExceptionMgr(useExceptions=True):
            try:
                dataset = gdal.OpenEx(path, gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER | gdal.OF_READONLY)
            except RuntimeError:
                return False
            try:
                group = dataset.GetRootGroup()
                names = set(group.GetMDArrayNames())
                conventions = _group_attributes(group).get(_CONVENTIONS, "")
            finally:
                dataset.Close()
        return _MPAS_TOKEN in str(conventions) and _VERTICES_ON_CELL in names

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read an MPAS grid into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The MPAS ``.nc`` file.
            lazy: Unused -- this driver reads only the topology, which is eager.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: The Voronoi dual as nodes plus mixed-degree face connectivity.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If a defining array is missing.
        """
        return _MpasReader(path).build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/_base.py 
def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override

    Args:

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: Nastran — bulk-data mesh
docs.text:
The Nastran bulk-data reader. A .bdf/.nas/.fem deck is a plain-text finite-element model: GRID cards give node coordinates and CTRIA3/CQUAD4 cards give the surface element-to-node lists. Node ids are arbitrary labels, resolved to contiguous indices through an id map rather than by assuming id == index + 1, so a gapped or renumbered deck wires correctly.

Driver name nastran Suffixes .bdf, .nas, .fem Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns MeshDataset

docs.title: Field layouts
docs.text:
Three card layouts share one deck and each line declares its own:

  • small fixed-field — ten 8-character columns;
  • large fixed-field — a * on the card name, 16-character columns spilling onto a * continuation line;
  • free field — comma-separated.

A fixed-field real may embed its exponent sign without an E — -2.45-16 means -2.45e-16, and 1.5D+3 (Fortran double) means 1500.0. All three spellings are parsed.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Volumetric and line elements are skipped — CTETRA/CPENTA/CHEXA/CPYRA solids and CBAR/CBEAM bars are dropped; only CTRIA3 and CQUAD4 surface faces are read. A genuine 3D mesh is out of scope (design §21.1), so a deck of only solids is refused for carrying no surface. CTRIA3 rows are fill-padded to the four columns of CQUAD4.
  • Node ids are arbitrary labels, mapped to contiguous 0-based indices with the 1-based base recorded for a writer. An element naming an id no GRID defines is refused, and a duplicate GRID id is ambiguous and refused.
  • Node elevation — the GRID X3 column becomes a node_z variable when any value is non-zero, matching the Exodus and gmsh readers; an all-zero column is dropped rather than kept as a meaningless node_z.
  • There is no CRS in the format — the coordinates are engineering coordinates with no datum — so crs is None.
  • The .fem suffix is shared with DHI FEFLOW. can_open requires the Nastran signature (a GRID and a CTRIA3/CQUAD4 card, and no FEFLOW PROBLEM:/CLASS header), so a FEFLOW .fem is declined rather than misread.

Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the Nastran bulk-data (.bdf/.nas/.fem) mesh format.

Builds the surface mesh from GRID nodes and CTRIA3/CQUAD4 faces. Node ids are arbitrary labels resolved through an id map, so a gapped or out-of-order deck wires correctly; the connectivity arrives 0-based with the bulk-data base recorded for a writer. CTRIA3 rows are fill-padded to the four columns of CQUAD4. Node elevation (the GRID X3 column) becomes a node_z variable when any value is non-zero, matching the Exodus and gmsh readers.

Documented limitations
  • Volumetric and line elements are skipped. CTETRA/CPENTA/CHEXA/ CPYRA solids and CBAR/CBEAM bars are dropped; only CTRIA3 and CQUAD4 surface faces are read. A genuine 3D mesh is out of scope (design section 21.1), so a deck of only solids is refused for having no surface.
  • Three field layouts are read -- small (8-column) and large (16-column) fixed-field, and free (comma-separated). A fixed-field real may embed its exponent sign without an E (-2.45-16 is -2.45e-16).
  • Node ids are arbitrary labels, mapped to contiguous indices; an element naming an id no GRID defines is refused, and a duplicate GRID id is ambiguous and refused.
  • Nastran carries no CRS -- the coordinates are engineering coordinates with no datum -- so crs is always None; it is never guessed.
  • The .fem suffix is shared with DHI FEFLOW. can_open requires the Nastran signature (a GRID and a CTRIA3/CQUAD4 card, no FEFLOW PROBLEM:/CLASS header), so a FEFLOW .fem is declined.
Example

Read a Nastran deck (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real deck)::

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("model.bdf")
mesh.mesh.n_node, mesh.mesh.n_face

class NastranDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the Nastran bulk-data (``.bdf``/``.nas``/``.fem``) mesh format.

    Builds the surface mesh from ``GRID`` nodes and ``CTRIA3``/``CQUAD4`` faces. Node ids
    are arbitrary labels resolved through an id map, so a gapped or out-of-order deck wires
    correctly; the connectivity arrives 0-based with the bulk-data base recorded for a
    writer. ``CTRIA3`` rows are fill-padded to the four columns of ``CQUAD4``. Node
    elevation (the ``GRID`` ``X3`` column) becomes a ``node_z`` variable when any value is
    non-zero, matching the Exodus and gmsh readers.

    Documented limitations:
        - **Volumetric and line elements are skipped.** ``CTETRA``/``CPENTA``/``CHEXA``/
          ``CPYRA`` solids and ``CBAR``/``CBEAM`` bars are dropped; only ``CTRIA3`` and
          ``CQUAD4`` surface faces are read. A genuine 3D mesh is out of scope (design
          section 21.1), so a deck of only solids is refused for having no surface.
        - **Three field layouts are read** -- small (8-column) and large (16-column)
          fixed-field, and free (comma-separated). A fixed-field real may embed its
          exponent sign without an ``E`` (``-2.45-16`` is ``-2.45e-16``).
        - **Node ids are arbitrary labels**, mapped to contiguous indices; an element
          naming an id no ``GRID`` defines is refused, and a duplicate ``GRID`` id is
          ambiguous and refused.
        - Nastran carries no CRS -- the coordinates are engineering coordinates with no
          datum -- so ``crs`` is always ``None``; it is never guessed.
        - The ``.fem`` suffix is shared with DHI FEFLOW. ``can_open`` requires the Nastran
          signature (a ``GRID`` and a ``CTRIA3``/``CQUAD4`` card, no FEFLOW
          ``PROBLEM:``/``CLASS`` header), so a FEFLOW ``.fem`` is declined.

    Example:
        Read a Nastran deck (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real deck)::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

            mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("model.bdf")
            mesh.mesh.n_node, mesh.mesh.n_face
    """

    name = "nastran"
    long_name = "Nastran bulk data"
    suffixes = (".bdf", ".nas", ".fem")
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is a Nastran deck, declining a FEFLOW ``.fem``.

        The file is scanned (short-circuiting as soon as both are seen) for a ``GRID``
        card and a ``CTRIA3``/``CQUAD4`` card; a FEFLOW ``PROBLEM:``/``CLASS`` header --
        the one real collision on the shared ``.fem`` suffix -- declines the file outright.
        The whole file is read because the ``GRID`` block precedes the element cards and a
        large node block must not push them past a fixed window. Bytes are decoded
        leniently, so a binary or empty file answers ``False`` rather than raising.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` only when both a ``GRID`` and a surface element card are found
                and no FEFLOW header appears.
        """
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            prefix = handle.read()
        has_grid = False
        has_face = False
        first_significant = True
        for raw in prefix.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace").splitlines():
            stripped = raw.strip()
            if not stripped or stripped.startswith(_COMMENT):
                continue
            upper = stripped.upper()
            # A FEFLOW .fem opens with PROBLEM:/CLASS; key the decline on the first
            # significant line only, so a Nastran line merely beginning with those words
            # deeper in the deck does not false-decline.
            if first_significant:
                first_significant = False
                if any(upper.startswith(marker) for marker in _FEFLOW_MARKERS):
                    return False
            keyword = _card_name(raw)
            if keyword == _GRID:
                has_grid = True
            elif keyword in _FACE_CARDS:
                has_face = True
            if has_grid and has_face:
                return True
        return has_grid and has_face

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a Nastran deck into a :class:`~pyramids_mesh._base.ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The deck to read.
            lazy: Ignored -- a bulk-data deck is plain text and read eagerly; accepted to
                match the driver protocol.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, the surface faces, and ``node_z`` when elevations are set.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the deck has no ``GRID`` card, no surface
                element, or a malformed field.
            ValueError: If an element references an undefined node id, or two ``GRID``
                cards share an id.
        """
        return _Deck(path).build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override
    this to read the names from the file.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path, unused by the single-mesh default.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The configured mesh name, as a one-item list.

    Examples:
        - A single-mesh driver names one topology, so the list it returns is the
          set of values ``read``'s ``mesh_name`` will accept:

            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> TinyDriver().mesh_names("anything.tiny")
            ['mesh2d']
    """
    return [self._default_mesh_name]

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.

            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so

            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)

            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )

            (3, 1)

            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: Netgen — volume mesh
docs.text:
The Netgen reader. It reads the Netgen .vol ASCII file (and its gzip-compressed .vol.gz form): a mesh3d preamble with a dimension and a geomtype setting, then one section per topology kind — each a keyword line, a count line, and that many rows. The file is parsed with the standard library alone — a line-record walk, through gzip for a compressed file — so the driver declares no dependency and never imports a mesh library.

Driver name netgen Suffixes .vol, .vol.gz Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns MeshDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("domain.vol")   # or domain.vol.gz

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Netgen lists each topology kind in its own section. The reader turns the surface triangles into faces and skips the rest:

Section Row Used for points x y z node coordinates (node_x, node_y, node_z) surfaceelements surfnr bcnr domin domout np p1…pnp the np trailing ids become a face volumeelements matnr np p1…p4 dropped (volumetric) materials, bcnames, edgesegmentsgi2, identifications, … — skipped (metadata)

A surfaceelements row carries four leading columns — the surface number, the boundary condition, and the two adjacent domains — then the node count np and that many 1-based node ids. Only the trailing ids are kept.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Only the surface becomes a mesh. The surfaceelements triangles become faces; the volumeelements tetrahedra are dropped rather than boundary-extracted. A faithful volume read needs the layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet, and reconstructing the boundary from the tetrahedra could not be verified against a sample, so the surface the file already lists is kept instead.
  • The optional trailing sections are metadata, not topology. materials, bcnames, identifications, edgesegmentsgi2 and the rest of the Netgen table are skipped; only points and surfaceelements are read.
  • The node z column is carried as a node_z variable, not as a coordinate — the mesh model is planar. Unlike the 2DM and VTK readers, a flat z = 0 is kept rather than omitted: Netgen is a 3D format whose points always declare a real elevation.
  • Node ids are 1-based. The connectivity arrives 0-based with the base 1 recorded for a writer. Values are eager — a .vol file is plain text with nothing to defer. There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseDriver

Reader for the Netgen .vol / .vol.gz mesh format.

Reads the points node coordinates and the surfaceelements triangles of a Netgen 3D mesh into a surface :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset. Node ids are 1-based and contiguous, so the connectivity arrives 0-based with the base recorded for a writer. The node z column becomes a node_z variable, since the pyramids mesh model is planar and carries no per-node elevation coordinate.

A plain .vol file is read as text; a .vol.gz file is decompressed through the standard-library :mod:gzip first. Both go through the same line-record walk.

Documented limitations
  • Only the surface becomes a mesh. The surfaceelements section (the mesh surface's triangles) is turned into faces; the volumeelements tetrahedra are dropped rather than boundary-extracted. A faithful volume read needs the layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet (design section 21.1), and reconstructing the boundary from the tetrahedra could not be verified against a sample, so the surface the file already lists is kept instead.
  • The optional trailing sections are metadata, not topology. materials, bcnames, identifications, edgesegmentsgi2 and the rest of the Netgen table are skipped; only points and surfaceelements are read.
  • The node z column is carried as a node_z variable, not as a coordinate -- the mesh model is planar. Unlike the 2DM and VTK readers, a flat z = 0 is kept rather than omitted: Netgen is a 3D format whose points always declare a real elevation.
  • Netgen carries no CRS, so crs is always None; it is never guessed from the coordinate magnitudes.

Examples:

  • Read the committed Netgen sample: 65 nodes and 108 surface triangles, with the 1-based connectivity arriving 0-based and the file's base recorded for a writer. (Shown, not run as a doctest -- it reads a committed data file.)::

    from pyramids_mesh.drivers.netgen import NetgenDriver

    dataset = NetgenDriver().read("tests/data/netgen/periodic_3d.vol") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face # (65, 108) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.original_start_index # 1 dataset.get("node_z").location # 'node'

class NetgenDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the Netgen ``.vol`` / ``.vol.gz`` mesh format.

    Reads the ``points`` node coordinates and the ``surfaceelements`` triangles of a
    Netgen 3D mesh into a surface :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset`. Node ids
    are 1-based and contiguous, so the connectivity arrives 0-based with the base
    recorded for a writer. The node ``z`` column becomes a ``node_z`` variable, since the
    pyramids mesh model is planar and carries no per-node elevation coordinate.

    A plain ``.vol`` file is read as text; a ``.vol.gz`` file is decompressed through the
    standard-library :mod:`gzip` first. Both go through the same line-record walk.

    Documented limitations:
        - **Only the surface becomes a mesh.** The ``surfaceelements`` section (the mesh
          surface's triangles) is turned into faces; the ``volumeelements`` tetrahedra
          are dropped rather than boundary-extracted. A faithful volume read needs the
          layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet (design section 21.1), and
          reconstructing the boundary from the tetrahedra could not be verified against a
          sample, so the surface the file already lists is kept instead.
        - **The optional trailing sections are metadata, not topology.** ``materials``,
          ``bcnames``, ``identifications``, ``edgesegmentsgi2`` and the rest of the Netgen
          table are skipped; only ``points`` and ``surfaceelements`` are read.
        - **The node ``z`` column is carried as a ``node_z`` variable**, not as a
          coordinate -- the mesh model is planar. Unlike the 2DM and VTK readers, a flat
          ``z = 0`` is kept rather than omitted: Netgen is a 3D format whose points always
          declare a real elevation.
        - Netgen carries no CRS, so ``crs`` is always ``None``; it is never guessed from
          the coordinate magnitudes.

    Examples:
        - Read the committed Netgen sample: 65 nodes and 108 surface triangles, with the
          1-based connectivity arriving 0-based and the file's base recorded for a writer.
          (Shown, not run as a doctest -- it reads a committed data file.)::

            from pyramids_mesh.drivers.netgen import NetgenDriver

            dataset = NetgenDriver().read("tests/data/netgen/periodic_3d.vol")
            dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face              # (65, 108)
            dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.original_start_index  # 1
            dataset.get("node_z").location                       # 'node'
    """

    name = "netgen"
    long_name = "Netgen volume mesh"
    suffixes = (".vol", ".vol.gz")
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file head carries the Netgen signature.

        A bounded prefix is read -- through :mod:`gzip` for a ``.vol.gz`` file -- and
        decoded leniently, so a binary, empty or truncated file answers ``False`` rather
        than raising. The prefix is scanned for a standalone ``mesh3d`` or
        ``surfaceelements`` line; matching the keyword rather than a substring keeps a
        file that merely mentions one in a comment from qualifying.

        This never raises: a decompression or decoding failure is reported as a decline,
        so a corrupt candidate cannot abort driver dispatch.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the signature is found in the sniffed prefix.
        """
        try:
            with _open_text(path) as handle:
                read = 0
                for line in handle:
                    read += len(line)
                    if read > _SNIFF_LIMIT:
                        break
                    stripped = line.strip()
                    if not stripped or stripped.startswith(_COMMENT):
                        continue
                    if stripped.split()[0].lower() in _SIGNATURE:
                        return True
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
            # A non-gzip file under a `.gz` name, a corrupt stream, or any decode trouble
            # is a decline, not an error: `can_open` must answer for every candidate.
            return False
        return False

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a Netgen ``.vol`` file into a :class:`~pyramids_mesh._base.ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ``.vol`` / ``.vol.gz`` file to read.
            lazy: Ignored -- a Netgen file is plain text and read eagerly.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, the fill-padded surface-triangle connectivity, and the
                node elevation as a ``node_z`` variable.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file carries no Netgen signature, declares
                no ``points`` or ``surfaceelements`` section, a section's count line is not
                an integer, a row is short of the columns it declares, or a numeric field
                is not a number.
        """
        scan = _Scan(path)
        scan.run()
        return scan.build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override
    this to read the names from the file.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path, unused by the single-mesh default.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The configured mesh name, as a one-item list.

    Examples:
        - A single-mesh driver names one topology, so the list it returns is the
          set of values ``read``'s ``mesh_name`` will accept:

            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> TinyDriver().mesh_names("anything.tiny")
            ['mesh2d']
    """
    return [self._default_mesh_name]

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network

            >>> import numpy as np

            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: OBJ — Wavefront OBJ
docs.text:
The Wavefront OBJ reader. ASCII v x y z vertices and 1-based f faces, hand-parsed — a geometry interchange format with elevation per vertex and no time axis.

No CRS, no georeferencing. OBJ carries no coordinate reference system or spatial reference of any kind, so crs is always None. That makes it a low-value format for a GIS stack; it is provided for mesh interchange only.

Driver name obj Suffixes .obj Capabilities read_mesh, read_data Extra required none Returns MeshDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("surface.obj")

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• A round trip is not geometrically faithful. z survives as a node_z variable, but pyramids' mesh model is planar, so a consumer reading the geometry sees the (x, y) projection. This is inherent to carrying a 3D surface in a 2D model (design §6).
  • OBJ carries no CRS and no georeferencing, so crs is None.
  • The whole file is read eagerly — a line-oriented text format has no record index to seek — so the driver does not declare lazy_data.
  • Faces may be triangles, quads or higher n-gons; short rows pad to the widest with -1. A face of fewer than three vertices is refused.
  • A face token may be a bare index or an index/texture/normal triple (f v/vt/vn); only the vertex index before the first / is used. Texture coordinates, vertex normals, grouping and material cards are read past and not carried.
  • Face indices are 1-based in OBJ and arrive 0-based, with the base recorded for a writer.
