docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override

    Args:

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

def write(self, dataset, path: str, **options) -> None:
    """Write a mesh back to a PLY file.

    Emits a ``vertex`` element of ``double x/y/z`` and a ``face`` element of a
    ``property list uchar int vertex_indices``, in ASCII (the default) or either
    binary byte order. Node elevation is taken from a node-located ``node_z``
    variable when present, else ``0``; face indices stay 0-based, as PLY requires.

    Arbitrary per-vertex properties the reader surfaced as node variables (colours,
    normals) are **not** written back -- only ``x``/``y``/``z`` -- so a round trip is
    geometrically faithful but drops those extras (design sections 6 and 20.3).

    Args:
        dataset: The :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` to write.
        path: The output ``.ply`` path.
        **options: ``format`` selects ``"ascii"`` (default),
            ``"binary_little_endian"`` or ``"binary_big_endian"``.

    Raises:
        FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the dataset carries no faces, or ``format`` is
            not one of the three PLY encodings.
    """
    mesh = dataset.mesh
    connectivity = mesh.face_node_connectivity
    if connectivity is None or connectivity.data is None:
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"cannot write {path!r}: the dataset has no face connectivity to write "
            f"as a PLY mesh"
        )
    fmt = options.get("format", "ascii")
    if fmt not in _PLY_FORMATS:
        raise FileFormatNotSupportedError(
            f"cannot write {path!r}: unknown PLY format {fmt!r}; use 'ascii', "
            f"'binary_little_endian' or 'binary_big_endian'"
        )
    node_x = np.asarray(mesh.node_x, dtype=np.float64)
    node_y = np.asarray(mesh.node_y, dtype=np.float64)
    node_z = _writer_node_z(dataset, len(node_x))
    faces = np.asarray(connectivity.data)
    _write_ply(path, fmt, node_x, node_y, node_z, faces)

docs.title: SCHISM — hgrid.gr3 horizontal grid
docs.text:
The SCHISM reader. SCHISM is an unstructured-grid hydrodynamic model whose horizontal grid is the ASCII hgrid.gr3: a node list (id, x, y, depth), a mixed triangle/quad element table (id, i34, n1, n2, n3[, n4]) and open/land boundary sections. The layout is the one ADCIRC's fort.14 uses, so the two readers share the node- and element-block parser.

Driver name schism Suffixes .gr3 Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns MeshDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("run/hgrid.gr3")

bed = mesh.get("node_z")                                   # SCHISM node depth
ocean = mesh.global_attributes["open_boundary_nodes"]      # 0-based node-id arrays
land = mesh.global_attributes["land_boundary_nodes"]

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Horizontal grid only. hgrid.gr3 carries the 2-D mesh and its node depth; SCHISM's vertical grid (vgrid.in) and results (schout_*.nc) are separate files and are not read here.
  • Triangles and quads. i34 is 3 (triangle) or 4 (quad); a mixed grid is returned as a quad-width face table whose triangle rows are fill-padded, the form pyramids expects. Any other element type is refused rather than guessed.
  • Node and element ids are 1-based — resolved to 0-based, the base recorded for a writer. Boundary node-id lists are likewise converted to 0-based so they index straight into the mesh.
  • No CRS. .gr3 declares no authority (the coordinates may be lon/lat or a projected system), so crs is None rather than guessed. depth is carried verbatim as node_z.
  • Boundaries become metadata, not topology. The open/land node lists are stored on global_attributes (open_boundary_nodes / land_boundary_nodes, with the counts n_open_boundaries / n_land_boundaries); they are not built into edge connectivity.

  • No CRS. .gr3 declares no authority (the coordinates may be lon/lat or a projected system), so crs is None rather than guessed. depth is carried verbatim as node_z.

Example

Read a SCHISM grid and reach its depth and boundary lists (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real hgrid.gr3)::

class SchismDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the SCHISM ``hgrid.gr3`` horizontal grid.

    The mesh comes from ``hgrid.gr3``: node coordinates, the node ``depth`` (becomes a
    ``node_z`` variable) and the 1-based element table, which may hold both triangles
    (``i34 == 3``) and quads (``i34 == 4``). A mixed grid is returned as a
    quad-width table whose triangle rows are fill-padded, the form pyramids expects. The
    open- and land-boundary node-id lists are parsed and carried as dataset metadata.

    Documented limitations:
        - **Horizontal grid only.** ``hgrid.gr3`` carries the 2-D mesh and its node
          depth; SCHISM's vertical grid (``vgrid.in``) and results (``schout_*.nc``) are
          separate files and are not read here.
        - **Node and element ids are 1-based** -- resolved to 0-based, the base recorded
          for a writer. Boundary node-id lists are likewise converted to 0-based so they
          index straight into the mesh.
        - **No CRS.** ``.gr3`` declares no authority (the coordinates may be lon/lat or a
          projected system), so ``crs`` is ``None`` rather than guessed. ``depth`` is
          carried verbatim as ``node_z``.
        - **Boundaries become metadata, not topology.** The open/land node lists are
          stored on ``global_attributes`` (``open_boundary_nodes`` /
          ``land_boundary_nodes``); they are not built into edge connectivity.

    Example:
        Read a SCHISM grid and reach its depth and boundary lists (shown, not run as a
        doctest -- it needs a real ``hgrid.gr3``)::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

            mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("run/hgrid.gr3")
            bed = mesh.get("node_z")                       # SCHISM node depth
            ocean = mesh.global_attributes["open_boundary_nodes"]  # 0-based node ids
    """

    name = "schism"
    long_name = "SCHISM"
    suffixes = (".gr3",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file opens as a ``.gr3`` grid.

        Shares :func:`pyramids_mesh.drivers._gr3.sniff_gr3` with the ADCIRC reader, since
        the header and first node line are identical between the two formats.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the header and first node line are grid-shaped.
        """
        return sniff_gr3(path)

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read an ``hgrid.gr3`` into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ``.gr3`` file.
            lazy: Unused -- the whole grid is read eagerly, as a ``.gr3`` is small and
                carries no deferred result series.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: The surface mesh, ``node_z`` and the boundary node lists as
                metadata.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If an element is neither a triangle nor a quad.
        """
        with open(path, encoding="latin-1") as handle:
            node_x, node_y, node_z, faces = read_gr3_grid(
                handle, allow_quads=True, source=path
            )
            open_boundaries, land_boundaries = _read_boundaries(handle)
        return ParsedMesh(
            node_x=node_x,
            node_y=node_y,
            faces=faces,
            fill_value=-1,
            # .gr3 node/element ids are 1-based; validate re-bases and records the base.
            start_index=1,
            node_z=node_z,
            crs=None,
            global_attributes={
                "source": "SCHISM hgrid.gr3",
                "n_open_boundaries": len(open_boundaries),
                "n_land_boundaries": len(land_boundaries),
                "open_boundary_nodes": open_boundaries,
                "land_boundary_nodes": land_boundaries,
            },
            topology_dimension=2,
            mesh_name="mesh2d",
        )

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """List the topology names in the file.

    A single-mesh format returns a one-item list; ``multi_mesh`` drivers override
    this to read the names from the file.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path, unused by the single-mesh default.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The configured mesh name, as a one-item list.

    Examples:
        - A single-mesh driver names one topology, so the list it returns is the
          set of values ``read``'s ``mesh_name`` will accept:

            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver

            ...     name = "tiny"

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded

            honour it.

            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.

            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither

            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)

            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )

            (3, 1)

            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)

          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read

            >>> import numpy as np

            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):

            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )

            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)

            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),

            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: SCRIP — remapping-grid NetCDF
docs.text:
The SCRIP reader. SCRIP (the Spherical Coordinate Remapping and Interpolation Package) describes a grid for remapping as NetCDF: every cell is given by its corner coordinates directly in grid_corner_lat/grid_corner_lon (shape grid_size × grid_corners), with grid_center_lat/grid_center_lon the cell centres. There is no shared node list — the same corner is repeated by every cell that touches it — so the driver deduplicates the corners into a node table and builds face-node connectivity into it. Read through the vendored GDAL multidimensional API (no declared dependency).

Driver name scrip Suffixes .nc Capabilities read_mesh Extra required none Returns MeshDataset

A SCRIP grid is not UGRID, so read_file reaches the driver through its NetCDF-suffix fallback:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("outCSne8.nc")   # corners -> shared nodes
mesh.mesh.n_face                               # the SCRIP cells

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• Corner dedup uses a rounded key, not float equality. Shared corners are matched after rounding to a fixed tolerance; raw float comparison would leave duplicate nodes and split edges. The unique nodes are sorted, so the same file gives the same node order every run.
  • A repeated corner marks padding. SCRIP fills a cell with fewer corners than the grid_corners width by repeating a corner; a corner that duplicates an earlier one in the same cell becomes -1 fill, so a triangle in a quad-width table yields a fill-padded three-node face. SCRIP repeats a trailing corner, so the padding lands in the tail of the row as pyramids requires.
  • Coordinates are carried in the file's unit, degrees by default. A units attribute naming radians is honoured and the coordinates converted to degrees; otherwise they are left as the file gave them.
  • No CRS. The grid is lon/lat on a sphere with no EPSG authority, so crs is None rather than guessed.
  • grid_imask is not used to drop cells. Every cell is kept; this driver declares read_mesh only and ships no variables.

Example

class ScripDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for SCRIP remapping-grid NetCDF.

    SCRIP stores each cell's corner coordinates (``grid_corner_lat``/``grid_corner_lon``)
    rather than a node list and connectivity. The driver deduplicates the corners into a
    shared node table and builds face-node connectivity into it, so a SCRIP grid becomes
    an ordinary :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset`. The cell centres
    (``grid_center_lat``/``grid_center_lon``) become the face centres.

    Documented limitations:
        - **Corner dedup uses a rounded key, not float equality.** Shared corners are
          matched after rounding to a fixed tolerance; raw float comparison would leave
          duplicate nodes and split edges. The unique nodes are sorted, so the same file
          gives the same node order every run.
        - **A repeated corner marks padding.** SCRIP fills a cell with fewer corners than
          the ``grid_corners`` width by repeating a corner; a corner that duplicates an
          earlier one in the same cell becomes ``-1`` fill, so a triangle in a quad-width
          table yields a fill-padded three-node face. SCRIP repeats a trailing corner, so
          the padding lands in the tail of the row as pyramids requires.
        - **Coordinates are carried in the file's unit, degrees by default.** A
          ``units`` attribute naming radians is honoured and the coordinates converted to
          degrees; otherwise they are left as the file gave them.
        - **No CRS.** The grid is lon/lat on a sphere with no EPSG authority, so ``crs``
          is ``None`` rather than guessed.
        - **``grid_imask`` is not used to drop cells.** The mask is read past but every
          cell is kept; this driver declares ``read_mesh`` only and ships no variables.

    Example:
        Read a SCRIP grid (shown, not run as a doctest -- it needs a real NetCDF file),
        reached through ``read_file``'s NetCDF fallback::

            from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

            mesh = MeshDataset.read_file("outCSne8.nc")   # corners -> shared nodes
            mesh.mesh.n_face                               # the SCRIP cells
    """

    name = "scrip"
    long_name = "SCRIP remapping grid"
    suffixes = (".nc",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is a SCRIP grid, by its corner arrays.

        Keyed on ``grid_corner_lat`` and ``grid_corner_lon``, which are unique to SCRIP,
        so a plain NetCDF or another model's ``.nc`` -- MPAS, ICON, ESMF, GEOS, 3Di or
        TUFLOW FV -- is not claimed. Opening a non-NetCDF file raises inside GDAL and is
        reported as "not SCRIP" rather than propagated.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when both corner arrays are present.
        """
        with gdal.ExceptionMgr(useExceptions=True):
            try:
                dataset = gdal.OpenEx(path, gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER | gdal.OF_READONLY)
            except RuntimeError:
                return False
            try:
                names = _group_names(dataset.GetRootGroup())
            finally:
                dataset.Close()
        return {_CORNER_LAT, _CORNER_LON} <= names

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a SCRIP grid into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The SCRIP ``.nc`` file.
            lazy: Unused -- this driver reads only the topology, which is eager.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes deduplicated from the cell corners, the face connectivity
                and the cell centres.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If a defining corner array is missing.
        """
        return _ScripReader(path).build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

    import os import tempfile from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) driver = TinyDriver() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny") ... open(empty, "wb").close() ... verdicts = ( ... driver.can_open(empty), ... driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")), ... driver.can_open(directory), ... ) verdicts (True, False, False)

  • A _sniff that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

    import os import tempfile import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "broken" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _sniff(self, path): ... raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong") with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny") ... with open(path, "wb") as handle: ... _ = handle.write(b"anything at all") ... with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: ... warnings.simplefilter("always") ... verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path) verdict False str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1] 'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'

Source code in src/pyramids_mesh/_base.py 
def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    A ``_sniff`` that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file
    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

    Examples:
        - The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the
          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()
            ...     verdicts = (
            ...         driver.can_open(empty),
            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),
            ...     )
            >>> verdicts
            (True, False, False)

        - A ``_sniff`` that raises never escapes: the file is declined and the
          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver
            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")
            ...     with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            ...         warnings.simplefilter("always")
            ...         verdict = BrokenSniffDriver().can_open(path)
            >>> verdict
            False
            >>> str(caught[0].message).split(" and ")[-1]
            'is treated as declining it: RuntimeError: header parser is wrong'
    """
    # Outside the guard on purpose: a bad argument type is the caller's error, not a
    # verdict about a file, so it propagates rather than becoming a warning.
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return False
    if not self._has_suffix(path):
        return False
    try:
        return self._sniff(path)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the contract is never to raise
        # Narrower than this (OSError alone) left the guarantee false for a _sniff
        # that hit a decoding or parsing error. Declining is the right answer, but
        # a driver whose sniff raises is a bug, so it is named rather than hidden.
        warnings.warn(
            f"{self.name or type(self).__name__} failed to sniff {path!r} and is "
            f"treated as declining it: {type(error).__name__}: {error}",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return False

def mesh_names(self, path: str) -> list[str]:

docs.title: read(path, *, mesh_name=None, lazy=True)
docs.text:
Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

Template method: _parse turns the file into a :class:ParsedMesh, validate_and_normalise enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is constructed into a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset -- or a :class:~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d when the topology is one-dimensional. Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The file to read.

required mesh_name str | None

Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh and a 1D network names them separately -- see mesh_names -- and this selects one. Note that Mesh1d has no name of its own, so on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded anywhere.

None lazy bool

Forwarded to _parse so a format with a real deferred loader can honour it.

True

Returns:

Type Description MeshDataset | Mesh1d

MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mesh_name is not one of the topologies mesh_names offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its _parse did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the file already defines, or on any invariant :func:~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise enforces.

Exception

Whatever _parse raises for a malformed file -- a format driver raises FileFormatNotSupportedError, which is pyramids' own type rather than one invented here.

Examples:

  • A driver implements _parse and inherits everything else. Here the file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither mistake can reach the caller:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), ... faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]), ... start_index=1, ... ) dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny") dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face (3, 1) dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 1, 0]]

  • A _parse reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tiny1d" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"}) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), ... edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), ... topology_dimension=1, ... ) network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny") network.n_node, network.n_edge (3, 2) network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

  • A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in network_edges, and mesh_name picks which of the two this read returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

    import numpy as np import warnings from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "tinymixed" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"}) ... ... def mesh_names(self, path): ... return ["mesh2d", "network1d"] ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]), ... ) driver = TinyMixedDriver() with warnings.catch_warnings(): ... warnings.simplefilter("ignore") ... surface = driver.read("both.tiny") ... channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[0, 1, 2]] channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist() [[2, 3]]

A multi_mesh driver must name its topologies, because mesh_name is checked against mesh_names: a name the driver does not offer is refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

  • Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather than an empty network:

    import numpy as np from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver): ... name = "surfaceonly" ... suffixes = (".tiny",) ... ... def _parse(self, path, *, lazy): ... return ParsedMesh( ... node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), ... node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), ... faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]), ... ) try: ... SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'

def read(
    self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
) -> MeshDataset | Mesh1d:
    """Read the file into a fully-built pyramids object.

    Template method: ``_parse`` turns the file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`,
    ``validate_and_normalise`` enforces pyramids' invariants, and the result is
    constructed into a :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.MeshDataset` -- or a
    :class:`~pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Mesh1d` when the topology is one-dimensional.
    Do not override it; a driver that bypasses validation loses every invariant.

    Args:
        path: The file to read.
        mesh_name: Which topology to build. A format carrying both a surface mesh
            and a 1D network names them separately -- see ``mesh_names`` -- and
            this selects one. Note that ``Mesh1d`` has no name of its own, so
            on the 1D path the value only chooses the topology; it is not recorded
            anywhere.
        lazy: Forwarded to ``_parse`` so a format with a real deferred loader can
            honour it.

    Returns:
        MeshDataset | Mesh1d: The built mesh, or a network for a 1D topology.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mesh_name`` is not one of the topologies ``mesh_names``
            offers for this file, if the driver offers a 1D topology its ``_parse``
            did not produce, if a synthesised variable would collide with one the
            file already defines, or on any invariant
            :func:`~pyramids_mesh._validate.validate_and_normalise` enforces.
        Exception: Whatever ``_parse`` raises for a malformed file -- a format
            driver raises ``FileFormatNotSupportedError``, which is pyramids' own
            type rather than one invented here.

    Examples:
        - A driver implements ``_parse`` and inherits everything else. Here the
          file is 1-based and its single face is wound clockwise; the template
          method re-bases the connectivity and reverses the face, so neither
          mistake can reach the caller:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[1, 2, 3]]),
            ...             start_index=1,
            ...         )
            >>> dataset = TinyDriver().read("anything.tiny")
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (3, 1)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 1, 0]]

        - A ``_parse`` reporting a one-dimensional topology builds a network
          instead, which is a separate type with edges rather than faces:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyNetworkDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tiny1d"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
            ...             edges=np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]),
            ...             topology_dimension=1,
            ...         )
            >>> network = TinyNetworkDriver().read("channels.tiny")
            >>> network.n_node, network.n_edge
            (3, 2)
            >>> network.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1], [1, 2]]

        - A file holding both a surface and a 1D network puts the latter in
          ``network_edges``, and ``mesh_name`` picks which of the two this read
          returns. Each read warns about the half it leaves behind:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> import warnings
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class TinyMixedDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "tinymixed"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...     capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "multi_mesh"})
            ...
            ...     def mesh_names(self, path):
            ...         return ["mesh2d", "network1d"]
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...             network_edges=np.array([[2, 3]]),
            ...         )
            >>> driver = TinyMixedDriver()
            >>> with warnings.catch_warnings():
            ...     warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            ...     surface = driver.read("both.tiny")
            ...     channels = driver.read("both.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            >>> surface.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2]]
            >>> channels.edge_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[2, 3]]

          A ``multi_mesh`` driver must name its topologies, because ``mesh_name``
          is checked against ``mesh_names``: a name the driver does not offer is
          refused rather than quietly resolved to something else.

        - Asking for the 1D topology of a file that has none is an error rather
          than an empty network:

            >>> import numpy as np
            >>> from pyramids_mesh._base import BaseDriver, ParsedMesh
            >>> class SurfaceOnlyDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "surfaceonly"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _parse(self, path, *, lazy):
            ...         return ParsedMesh(
            ...             node_x=np.array([0.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
            ...             node_y=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
            ...             faces=np.array([[0, 1, 2]]),
            ...         )
            >>> try:
            ...     SurfaceOnlyDriver().read("flat.tiny", mesh_name="network1d")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            surfaceonly does not offer a 'network1d' topology in 'flat.tiny'
    """
    parsed = self._parse(path, lazy=lazy)
    parsed = validate_and_normalise(parsed)
    return self._construct(parsed, path=path, mesh_name=mesh_name)

docs.title: Selafin / Serafin — TELEMAC
docs.text:
The TELEMAC Selafin reader, and the package's first binary driver. Fortran unformatted records with an undeclared byte order and an optional double-precision variant. It proves the lazy path: the topology and the one-float time records are read eagerly, and each variable's per-timestep slab is left behind a loader that seeks straight to it.

Driver name selafin Suffixes .slf, .srf, .ser, .sel Capabilities read_mesh, read_data, lazy_data, write_mesh, write_data Extra required none Returns MeshDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import MeshDataset

dataset = MeshDataset.read_file("model.slf")
depth = dataset.get("WATER DEPTH").data   # read now; deferred until this line

dataset.to_file("copy.slf", driver="selafin")                 # lossless double precision
dataset.to_file("small.slf", driver="selafin", precision="single")  # smaller, lossy

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
The writer emits the same Fortran-record layout the reader parses, so a read → write → read round trip preserves the nodes, the connectivity (and its recorded 1-based IKLE base), the variable names and units, and the time steps.

  • Only node-located variables are written — the format has no face-located storage.
  • Every face must share a vertex count: Selafin stores a single element width (NDP), so a mixed tri/quad mesh is refused rather than written with a scrambled IKLE.
  • precision is "double" (the default — float64, a lossless round trip) or "single" (float32, smaller but lossy). A dataset with no face connectivity is refused.

docs.title: How it is read
docs.text:
• Byte order is detected, not declared. The first record must announce an 80-byte title in one order or the other; a file that does neither is not Selafin.
  • Precision comes from the title marker. SERAFIND is double precision, SERAFIN single, and the width applies to every float record — coordinates and data alike.
  • Variable names are 32 characters, split by position into a 16-char name and a 16-char unit. Splitting on whitespace instead would lose a multi-word name's tail.
  • IKLE connectivity is 1-based; it arrives 0-based, with the base recorded for a writer to restore.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The coordinate origin is applied, and getting it wrong is undetectable. IPARAM[2] and IPARAM[3] are the x and y origins the stored coordinates are offsets from; they are added to the node coordinates. Read without adding them, the mesh sits near zero instead of at its real location — plausible and completely wrong, with nothing in the data to catch it.
  • A layered 3D file is refused. IPARAM[6] is the plane count; 0 and 1 both mean 2D, and a value above 1 is a real 3D file. Its NPOIN and prism IKLE cannot be read as a flat 2D mesh without returning all planes' nodes under 6-node faces, and a faithful surface extraction needs a vendor file to verify the plane ordering, so it is refused rather than read as a malformed 2D mesh. A full 3D read needs the layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet (design §21.1).
  • A parallel sub-domain file is refused. A non-zero interface-point count (IPARAM[8]) means local numbering within one partition, so the connectivity would index a sub-domain rather than the whole mesh. It is keyed on interface points alone — the boundary-point field is a mesh property, nonzero for ordinary serial meshes. Merge the partitions before reading.
  • Variables are node-located, always — never inferred from an array length.
  • The IKLE row/column order could not be checked against a vendor file. It is read row-major (one element's NDP node ids contiguous), as the format specifies. A real file that stored it transposed would give a scrambled mesh; this is the detail a vendor sample should confirm, tracked for the vendor_data suite.
  • A partial final timestep is dropped with a warning — a run killed mid-write leaves a dangling time record, and only whole steps are read.
  • There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None; it is never inferred from the coordinate magnitudes.
